Nong Khai is a small town on the Mekong, right on the border with Laos, looking across to Vientiane on the far bank. Most visitors spend the late afternoon strolling along the river, catching the breeze at the Naga Plaza and the walking street, then drop by Tha Sadet Market for snacks and gifts brought over from Laos. In town, Wat Pho Chai houses Luang Pho Phra Sai, the city's most revered Buddha image, and Sala Kaew Ku is packed with giant, oddly captivating concrete sculptures. Come the end of Buddhist Lent, people from across the region gather to watch the Naga fireballs rise from the river. Nong Khai is an easy place to wander — riverside, temples, markets — and it's also the gateway across the Friendship Bridge into Laos for a day trip.
